title: Reading a raw response
description:
Take apart an HTTP response written as text.

```
status 200 (OK)
content-type: application/json
3 headers
body: {'id': 7, 'name': 'Ada'}
```

starter.main.py:
import json

raw = """HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r
Content-Type: application/json\r
Content-Length: 24\r
X-Request-Id: abc123\r
\r
{"id": 7, "name": "Ada"}"""


def parse(raw):
    return {"status": 0, "reason": "", "headers": {}, "body": None}


print(parse(raw))

hints: `head, _, body = raw.partition("\r\n\r\n")` splits the headers from the body (lesson 1.02).
requirements: Split the status line, the headers and the body (separated by a blank line).
Header names are case-insensitive: store them in lower case.
Parse the body with `json.loads` only when the content type is JSON.
stretch: Handle a body sent with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, which this course does not teach: look up chunked transfer coding (RFC 9112, section 7.1). Each chunk is its size in hexadecimal on its own line, then that many bytes; a chunk of size 0 ends the body.
